rows: MINERAL PROSPECTS OF WEST BENGAL DIRECTORATE OF MINES & MINERALS GOVERNMENT OF WEST BENGAL -- 1 of 19 -- THE ORGANISATION The Directorate of Mines and Minerals is a multidisciplinary technical organization to monitor systematic and scientific exploration and sustainable development of mineral resources of the state to promote mineral based industries, to encourage employment generation and to increase revenue earnings. The directorate is comprised of eight district offices with its Head office at Kolkata, West Bengal. It functions with both technical and administrative manpower. It carries out geological study, detail exploration work including drilling work to establish mineral deposits in the state. It processes mining lease applications, does royalty assessment for coal and other minerals including minor minerals. It also monitors the CBM and other natural gas projects toward revenue collection. It also acts as a task force to prevent illegal mining activities in the state. It is also the nodal agency for the state to interact with NMET and other Geological agencies of GOI such as GSI, ONGC, IBM etc. In West Bengal, DMM is the nodal agency and responsible for Exploration to Mine Closure through intermediate development of the minerals. -- 2 of 19 -- organogram Directorate of Mines & Minerals (HO) Geological Prospecting Branch Mining Estate Branch Superintending Geologist G.P. Lignite – Purba Bardhaman, and Birbhum districts. Granite – Several locations of Younger granites are reported from Purulia and Bankura District. Ceasium – GSI has already estimated about 0.1 Million tons of Ceasium bearing rocks. Apatite– different locations of Purulia District– Beldih, Panrkidih, Chirugora, Kutni & Purdaha. Blackstone – Extensive areas of Birbhum, Purulia and Bankura districts. More than 2 Billion Cum of Blackstone resources are available. Base Metals( Lead , Zinc & Copper)– Gorubathan/ Kalimpong and Purulia district,. Workable deposits at Kalimpong. Talc & Steatite –Gok-Karmi area and Lepcha Basti- Singlabazar area, Darjeeling District. Nearly 1.20 lakh tons. Limestone – Purulia and Bankura districts. Sand – Estimated Sand reserve across the state is more than 12 Mcum. Tungsten - Chandapatthar, Ratanpur, Chatradanga, Bankura District. Dolomite – Around 1 Million Tons in Purulia district and river bed deposits of North Bengal. Besides the above, occurrences of Lignite, Gold, Vanadium, Mica, Wolfram are also reported. Quartz & Feldspar – Purulia, Bankura, Jhargram and Birbhum districts. China Clay & Fire Clay – Around 6 Million Tons of Reserves estimated in Birbhum, Bankura and Purulia districts. -- 5 of 19 -- Oil & Gas occurrences of West Bengal  CBM extraction is ongoing at Raniganj East Block. After obtaining this datas MECL will formulate this exploration proposal and the cost estimates of the said blocks and submit it to the State Govermnments for comments. After completion of this projects and settlement, State Government shall auction the blocks as per the provisions of the Minerals (Auction Rules, 2015). -- 14 of 19 -- A. SAND DISTRICT NO.
